metadata.description: Sources for developer contribution quality analysis covering commit-level metrics, code quality measurement, AI attribution, and engineering productivity frameworks.
metadata.title: Contribution Quality Analysis - Sources

developer_productivity_research.name: DX Core 4: Measuring Developer Productivity
developer_productivity_research.relevance: Unified framework replacing standalone DORA/SPACE with four oppositional dimensions (speed, effectiveness, quality, impact). Current standard for productivity measurement.

developer_productivity_research.name: DORA 2024 Accelerate State of DevOps Report
developer_productivity_research.relevance: Industry benchmarks for delivery metrics. Finding: 7.2% stability decrease per 25% AI adoption increase — critical calibration data.

developer_productivity_research.name: SPACE of Developer Productivity
developer_productivity_research.relevance: Five-dimension framework (Satisfaction, Performance, Activity, Communication, Efficiency) that underpins DX Core 4.

developer_productivity_research.name: GitHub Octoverse 2025
developer_productivity_research.relevance: 986M pushes analyzed. Provides baseline norms for commit frequency, PR size, and review patterns across the industry.

code_quality_measurement.name: GitClear Diff Delta Methodology
code_quality_measurement.relevance: Proprietary commit-level quality metric classifying line changes into 7 operations. The closest thing to ground-truth commit quality scoring.

code_quality_measurement.name: GitClear AI Code Quality Research 2025
code_quality_measurement.relevance: 211M lines analyzed (2020-2024). Key data: duplication +48%, refactoring -60%, churn +84%. Defines the quality baseline for AI-era commits.

code_quality_measurement.name: CodeScene Behavioral Code Analysis
code_quality_measurement.relevance: Code Health scores (25+ factors, 1-10 scale) combined with git activity. Hotspot methodology for identifying high-risk code areas.

code_quality_measurement.name: SonarSource Cognitive Complexity
code_quality_measurement.relevance: Defines cognitive complexity as alternative to cyclomatic complexity. Better alignment with how developers process code mentally.

ghost_engineering_research.name: Stanford Ghost Engineer Study
ghost_engineering_research.relevance: 50,000+ engineers at 100+ companies. 9.5% ghost engineers. Methodology: simulates 10-expert panel per commit (r=0.82 with expert judgment).

ghost_engineering_research.name: METR AI Developer Productivity Study (arxiv 2507.09089)
ghost_engineering_research.relevance: RCT, 16 developers, 246 tasks. Developers felt 20% faster but were actually 19% slower with early-2025 tools (CI: +2% to +39%). Follow-up (Feb 2026) found unreliable signal due to recruitment issues — effect uncertain for latest tools.

ghost_engineering_research.name: DORA 2025: State of AI-Assisted Software Development
ghost_engineering_research.relevance: 90% AI adoption reported; AI adoption now correlates with higher throughput (reversal from 2024). New 7-archetype methodology replaces low/medium/high/elite clusters. Core finding: AI is a 'mirror and multiplier' of existing team strengths/dysfunctions. Does NOT contain the 54%/242.7%/66.2% bug-incident-epic figures commonly cited alongside it — those are Faros AI's, see below.

ghost_engineering_research.name: Faros AI: AI Engineering Report 2026 — The Acceleration Whiplash
ghost_engineering_research.relevance: Proprietary telemetry across 22,000+ developers / 4,000+ teams (not survey-based like DORA). Bugs per developer +54%, incidents per PR +242.7%, epics completed per developer +66%. Frequently misattributed to the DORA 2025 report in secondary coverage — verify attribution before citing as 'DORA'.

ai_attribution_and_detection.name: Agent Trace Specification
ai_attribution_and_detection.relevance: Vendor-neutral RFC for recording AI vs. human contributions at file and line level. Four contributor types: human, AI, mixed, unknown.

ai_attribution_and_detection.name: Agent Blame (Mesa)
ai_attribution_and_detection.relevance: Open-source line-level AI attribution for git repos. Hooks intercept AI edits from Cursor, Claude Code, OpenCode. Apache 2.0.

ai_attribution_and_detection.name: Git AI Attribution Tool
ai_attribution_and_detection.relevance: Open-source git extension tracking AI-generated code. Provides AI Blame, acceptance rate analytics, and multi-agent support.

ai_attribution_and_detection.name: Fingerprinting AI Coding Agents on GitHub
ai_attribution_and_detection.relevance: 33,580 PRs, 97.2% F1-score in agent identification using 41 features. Most discriminative: multiline commit ratio (44.7%), change concentration (10.1%).

ai_attribution_and_detection.name: Pangram Labs AI Code Detector
ai_attribution_and_detection.relevance: Commercial AI code detector using AST analysis, token probability, entropy measurement, neural fingerprinting. CI/CD API available.

ai_attribution_and_detection.name: Veracode GenAI Code Security Report 2025
ai_attribution_and_detection.relevance: Tested 100+ LLMs across 4 languages and 80 tasks. 45% of AI-generated code fails security checks; AI code has 2.74x more XSS vulnerabilities than human-written code. Authoritative source for AI security quality claims. Does NOT report the 1.75x logic-error figure (that is CodeRabbit's, see below) — do not conflate the two sources.

ai_attribution_and_detection.name: CodeRabbit AI vs. Human PR Quality Analysis (Dec 2025)
ai_attribution_and_detection.relevance: Analysis of 470 real pull requests. AI-authored PRs show 1.75x more logic/correctness errors than human-authored PRs. Frequently miscited as a Veracode finding — verify attribution before quoting.

commit_and_pr_practices.name: Google Engineering Practices: Small CLs
commit_and_pr_practices.relevance: Defines the standard for small, focused change lists. Basis for PR size scoring thresholds.

commit_and_pr_practices.name: Google Engineering Practices: CL Descriptions
commit_and_pr_practices.relevance: Standard for commit/CL description quality. Basis for commit message quality scoring.

commit_and_pr_practices.name: Git SubmittingPatches
commit_and_pr_practices.relevance: Official Git guidance on patch submission quality. Foundational reference for commit discipline metrics.

commit_and_pr_practices.name: Conventional Commits Specification
commit_and_pr_practices.relevance: Standard format for structured commit messages. Used in commit message quality scoring.

code_review_practices.name: Google Engineering Practices: Code Review Speed
code_review_practices.relevance: Defines review responsiveness expectations. Basis for D4 review responsiveness scoring.

code_review_practices.name: Conventional Comments
code_review_practices.relevance: Machine-parseable review comment intent labels. Reference for review depth analysis.

code_review_practices.name: PRPulse: PR Metrics That Predict Team Velocity
code_review_practices.relevance: Concrete benchmarks: time to first review (elite < 2h), PR size (elite < 250 LOC), review depth thresholds.

engineering_metrics_and_benchmarks.name: Qodo: Code Quality Metrics 2026
engineering_metrics_and_benchmarks.relevance: Eight measurable review quality signals including turnaround time, comment depth, and review duration benchmarks.

engineering_metrics_and_benchmarks.name: DX: Why Cyclomatic Complexity Misleads
engineering_metrics_and_benchmarks.relevance: Argues cognitive complexity better predicts developer effort than cyclomatic complexity. Supports D2 metric choice.

engineering_metrics_and_benchmarks.name: Jellyfish: Are 10% Actually Ghost Engineers?
engineering_metrics_and_benchmarks.relevance: Industry response to Stanford ghost engineering study with practical measurement approaches for engineering leaders.

clean_code_standards.name: Clean Code Standard (CC-* Rules)
clean_code_standards.relevance: Internal shared-skill rubric with stable CC-* rules used for commit sampling; not an external source.

clean_code_standards.name: OWASP Top Ten 2025
clean_code_standards.relevance: Security vulnerability baseline referenced by CC-SEC rules. Used in security-sensitive file change assessment.
